paper.title: Aspirin use and bleeding events during thrombocytopenia after autologous stem-cell transplantation for multiple myeloma.

source.title: Aspirin use and bleeding events during thrombocytopenia after autologous stem-cell transplantation for multiple myeloma.

study.setting: Heidelberg inpatient ASCT for multiple myeloma, 2011 to February 2020
exclusions: 13 patients who stopped ASA earlier than day+1 excluded from main analyses
study.ASAExposure: 75-100 mg at physician discretion; at least one dose after reinfusion day0, continued until at least day+1
study.plateletInhibitionAssumed: No turnover until hematopoietic recovery and inhibited host platelets after last ASA; transfusion may reverse effect
study.recommenceAsReported: Usually platelet count >20-50 x10^9/L; recommendations figure uses >50, not a tested uniform restart threshold
study.primaryOutcome: Documented bleeding during hospital stay, staged CTCAE5/BSMS/WHO
study.transfusionStrategies: Physician discretion prophylactic <10 x10^9/L or therapeutic bleeding signs; not assignable for every transfusion and omitted from model
study.statisticalMethods: Welch t/chi-square; univariate logistic then stepwise multivariable; Firth confirmation in separate supplement; PLTX model excludes bleeders, thrombocytopenia-duration model excludes bleeders and two outliers

results.outcome: In-hospital bleeding among physician-selected ASA users and controls

sourceQualifications.description: Retrospective EMR cohort with 57 ASA users and 1056 controls, physician-selected ASA and transfusion management. Groups differ in age, sex, HCT-CI and CV diseases. No randomized continuation/cessation strategy or causal safety/equivalence.

52/57 ASA users had secondary CV prevention indication, 5 primary. Controls include 30 secondary and 3 primary indications without ASA. This is not an aspirin myeloma antitumor or uniform IMiD primary VTE prophylaxis trial.

Outpatient ASCT, dual APT and therapeutic anticoagulation excluded; 13 early ASA pauses excluded from main analyses, separately discussed. Available single-center patients do not establish universal transplant safety or independent unique cross-corpus N.

75-100 mg at physician discretion, dose after day0/at least day+1 used to assume platelet inhibition, not measured function. Most41/57 stopped within20-50 x10^9/L with non-daily measurements. Usually restart >20-50 in methods versus >50 in Figure4; not a uniform tested threshold or continuous intake throughout aplasia.

Bleeding3/57 versus20/1056,5.3% versus1.9%,P.082; ASA OR2.78 CI.83-9.98 P.096 is univariate, not multivariable ASA estimate. Multivariable nonsignificance described but exact ASA/Firth estimate in unchecked supplement. Wide CI allows clinically important harm, not equal safety or no effect.

23 patients with bleeding in hospital, every bleed documented once rather than bleeding patient-days. Median onsetday+6 range-2 to+40 includes pre-transplant event.16BSMS clinicallysignificant events not all23 severe/major. Mild bleeding underreporting likely; postdischarge MACE not reliably assessed.

Two retinal bleeds among main57ASA, third retinal bleed in excluded early-pause group, not3/57. Main ASA casesday-2 atnormal170,day+6 PLC5 after2daypause,day+9 epistaxisPLC5 after3daypause; residual inhibition assumed not measured. Possible retinal causal concern attributed, not proven.

GI-history adjusted bleeding OR24.230 CI5.653-103.861 in text versus24.23 CI5.563-103.861 Figure2E. Text backward-selection versus figure forward-selection and text references Figure1E versus actualFigure2E. Retain literal discrepancy, no repaired CI or new adjusted ASA estimate.

Bleeding model durationPLC<=50 OR1.166 CI1.066-1.277 P<.001; diarrhea4.038 CI1.693-9.632 P.002; GI-history24.23 wide CI from only12history patients, possible overestimate. Few23events, stepwise models and many tested factors, multiplicity correction not stated; Firth supplement not checked.

Platelet unitsASA1.32SD1.42/control.78SD.96; textP<.001 versusTable2P.007 unresolved. Physician-selected extra transfusions may affect bleeding/inhibition; strategies unassignable, cannot conclude ASA independently caused extra transfusions or that they prevented no bleeds. PRBC means.86/.68 P.354 nonsignificance not equivalence.

DurationPLC<50 mean7.44/6.89daysP.174, <20 3.3/2.89P.146, <10 1.05/.88P.223. Duration prediction R2.113 adjusted.109 weak, excludes bleeders/two outliers, different from bleeding-risk model. PTTbeta.103 P>.001 and sumscoreOR1.194CI.731-19.52 literal odd values retained, not repaired or statistically upgraded.

Figure1 patient1 HCT-CI3 diagram versus6 caption retained as discrepancy; not silently harmonized. Figure/caption day-2 platelet170 versus overall bleeding maximum179 could represent source-specific values, not assumed typo or extra patient.

Three MACE during hospitalization, none with ASA or indication. No MACE during observed ASA pause does not establish withdrawal safety/protection, underpowered rare events, no reliable postdischarge capture. External 46%/one-in36 withdrawal estimate is cited background, not an effect measured here.

Authors say appears safe at20-50 x10^9/L yet harm cannot be excluded and results hypothesis-generating; Figure5 stronger safe language is attributed not adopted. Onlyone continuous-aplasia patient, no safety inference below20. Figure4 management algorithm rationale, not randomized evidence or current clinical recommendation here.
